chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Idrees, from Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Yahya bin Imran al-Ash'ari, that he said: We were told by Ibrahim bin Ishaq, from Amr [and] bin Ishaq, that he said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked:

What is the limitation of the weakened individual whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious, mentioned? He said: The one who is unable to (properly recite) a chapter of the Qur'an, when Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has created him in a manner that he should not be one who is unable to (do so).

key_terms.يُحْسِنُ: To be proficient or skilled in

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of the 'weakened' person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defining the 'weakened' (al-mustad'af) not merely as physically weak, but as one who lacks the capacity to master even a single chapter of the Qur'an, despite being created with the inherent potential for it. This definition highlights the spiritual and intellectual dimension of weakness in Shia exegesis, linking the inability to engage with divine revelation to a state of spiritual vulnerability. It underscores the importance of *ta'lim* (instruction) and *ta'wil* (interpretation) as means to elevate the believer from this state of 'weakening' to one of spiritual strength.
